clone_manifest_note: One entry per clone of each sweep; instance ids are positional (clone-<role>-<arch>-<index>).
concordance_note: One value per suite: every clone of both architectures of the concordance sweep reported the same raw and adjusted F1 and the same tuple counts (F1 is deterministic per binary and architecture-independent), equal to the paired run's. The README's "Current release" table renders these values from this record. Adjusted F1 is 1.0 on every suite. Raw F1 on s07 and s08 is lower than v0.2.0's: the tuples of classes 10 and 11 of docs/intended-divergences.md (a gVCF <NON_REF> block written as one intergenic_variant row; a breakend's mate described at the mate coordinate) leave the raw intersection, no other tuple does, and raw F1 sets nothing aside.
dataset_inventory_sha256_note: One value per sweep, identical across its clones of both architectures (each clone entry carries its own). The concordance sweep's clones also synced the archived Perl ground truth the comparator reads, so its inventory covers more files than the wall-time sweep's.
harness_skip_fields_note: The per-column field comparator was not run on the clones; it ran on one host's paired run of the previous release and this one on the same inputs, whose F1 per suite equals the clones'.
methodology_note: r8gd.8xlarge (ARM Graviton4) and r8id.8xlarge (Intel x86_64), 32 vCPU / 256 GiB / local NVMe instance store, spec-matched; 20 fresh clones per architecture booting the stock AL2023 base image, each syncing the dataset to local NVMe. The wall-time sweep runs scripts/concordance/run_clone_measurement.sh --walltime-only (--fork 16, sites-only inputs): one cold-cache warmup (discarded) and one timed measurement per cell, then self-terminates; median and P5/P95 across the clones per cell (Weibull, R type 6). The concordance sweep runs the same script without --walltime-only, so each clone also computes the ten-suite concordance report against the archived Perl ground truth; its wall times are not used, because the comparator running between suites perturbs the timed run that follows a warmup on the largest output.
per_cell_aggregates_note: Wall time per (arch, suite) over the completed clones of the wall-time sweep (median and quantiles by the Weibull estimator, R type 6); each of those clones' entry under clones carries the per-suite wall time it reported (wall_time_sec), so every aggregate re-derives from this record. The README's "Current release" table renders these values.
public_build_inputs_note: Git object ids of the build inputs at source_commit (crates tree, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, .cargo/config.toml), re-derived by the build host from the extracted source and recorded with the binary; a tag whose inputs equal these carries the code that was measured.
rustc_note: The compiler of the measured binaries, read from the build markers of both architectures; it is the toolchain the release workflow pins, so the release assets are builds of the same source, lockfile and compiler, identified by their own digests in SHA256SUMS.

same_day_control.note: Both binaries under the release protocol on the same day (--walltime-only, the discarded warmup's output flushed and deleted before the timed run), on the same instance types and images: the released version (20 + 20 clones) and the previous release (3 + 3 clones) agree within 6.2% in median wall time on 13 of 16 cells and within 1.8% in median user CPU time on every cell above 60 CPU-seconds; on the other 3 the released version is faster (s07 arm64 runs at 0.883 of the previous release's median; s08 arm64 runs at 0.459 of the previous release's median; s08 x86_64 runs at 0.606 of the previous release's median): the deletion-shaped evaluation of a breakend span borrows the variant instead of copying it per transcript.

scope: vep-rs alone: the released version's ten-suite concordance and its own wall times on both architectures, stated in the README beside the paper's figures, which do not change. Perl VEP and fastVEP are not re-measured, and no ratio against the paper's medians is stated: the release protocol deletes the discarded warmup's output before the timed run and the paper's did not. The same-day control below is the comparison the README cites.
sites_only_note: Every timed input is sites-only; s09 and s10 are pointer suites into the per-file structural-variant results of s07 and s08.
warmup_output_discarded_note: Before each timed run the harness flushes and deletes the discarded warmup's output (scripts/concordance/run_clone_measurement.sh, discard_warmup_output), so the timed run starts with the memory the warmup had.
